related_questions.question: What is the basic care of an eye injury?

text_blocks.snippet: Basic care for an eye injury includes immediately flushing the eye with water for at least 15 minutes if a chemical splash is involved, and covering the eye with a rigid shield (like a paper cup) if a cut or puncture is suspected. For blows to the eye, apply a cold compress without pressure. In all cases of serious injury, seek professional medical help promptly.

list.snippet: Flush immediately: Use water (or any drinkable liquid) to flush the eye for at least 15 minutes.
Keep the eye open: Wide open if possible during flushing.
Seek medical attention: Even after flushing, get professional medical help.
Don't flush: Avoid washing the eye with water or other liquids.
Cover with shield: Use a rigid shield (like a paper cup) to protect the eye.
Don't remove objects: If an object is stuck in the eye, do not attempt to remove it.
Seek medical attention: Get professional medical help promptly.

list.title: Apply cold compress:
list.snippet: Use a cold compress (not directly on the skin) to reduce pain and swelling.

list.title: Seek medical attention:
list.snippet: If there's pain, blurred vision, or other concerning symptoms, seek professional medical help immediately.
Don't rub: Avoid rubbing the eye, as this can worsen the injury.
Try to flush: If the object is visible and easily removable, try to flush it out with water or a commercial eyewash.
Seek medical attention: If the object doesn't come out easily or if you experience pain or vision changes, seek professional medical help.
Stay calm: Maintaining a calm demeanor can help the injured person stay cooperative.
Assess the situation: Determine the type and severity of the injury.
Don't bandage: Avoid bandaging the eye unless specifically instructed by a medical professional.
Seek professional help: For any severe injury or if you are unsure about the appropriate course of action, seek professional medical help immediately, according to first aid resources.

related_questions.question: What three things should you never do if a person has an eye injury?
related_questions.title: A few important things to remember when eye injuries occur:
list: Never touch, rub or apply pressure to your eye.
Never attempt to remove an object stuck in your eye.
Don't apply ointment or medication to your eye.
See a doctor as soon as possible, preferably an optometrist or an ophthalmologist.

text_blocks.snippet: For basic first aid, immediately flush the eye with water or another drinkable liquid for at least 15 minutes, keeping the eye open as wide as possible. Avoid rubbing the eye, and if a foreign body is present, try to let tears wash it out or use a commercial eyewash, but do not use tweezers. Seek emergency medical care promptly, especially if there's pain, vision changes, or if the object can't be easily removed.

list.title: Chemical Exposure:
list.snippet: Flush the eye immediately and copiously with water for at least 20 minutes. Do not use chemical cooling packs. Seek immediate medical attention and try to document the chemical involved.

list.title: Blows to the Eye:
list.snippet: Apply a cold compress (a cloth-wrapped ice pack) without pressure to the area around the eye to reduce swelling. Elevate the head to help reduce swelling.

list.title: Foreign Objects:
list.snippet: If a speck or small particle is present, try to flush it out with water or saline solution. If it's embedded or cannot be removed, seek immediate medical help.

list.title: Black Eye:
list.snippet: Apply a cold compress as soon as possible to reduce swelling. After 48 hours, warm compresses may help relieve pain.
Always seek professional medical advice: for any eye injury, even if it seems minor, as some injuries may not be immediately apparent.
Do not attempt to remove deeply embedded objects or use sharp objects: (like tweezers) to remove foreign bodies.
Avoid rubbing the eye: as this can cause further damage.
Monitor for signs of infection: (increased pain, redness, discharge) and seek immediate medical attention if these develop, according to the American Red Cross.
Keep the injured person calm: and explain what you are doing during the first aid process, according to ProFirstAid.
Be prepared to transport the injured person: to a medical facility, especially if the injury is severe.
